focal_entities.audience: the user approving the architecture at the design sign-off, and whoever builds the tool and its tests to it

goal_orientation.purpose: approving how the tool is put together to keep every file from being deleted, renamed or overwritten and to keep the record of a run, then building each part and its tests by it

goal_orientation.serves: AC1: Installed from this repository with `pipx install .`, the tool runs from any directory as a command of its own, such as `organize-downloads`, with Python 3 on macOS and Linux, and `pipx uninstall` removes it.
AC2: By default the tool works on the `Downloads` folder under the user's home; given another folder, it works on that folder instead.
AC3: Run without being told to move, the tool shows each file it would move with the kind folder it would go to, and changes nothing in the folder.
AC4: Told to move, the tool moves each file directly in the folder whose extension is in its built-in table into the folder of that kind: images, documents, archives, audio, video or installers.

AC5: In a run of AC3 or of AC4 these stay where they are and are shown as left in place: a file whose name is already taken in its kind folder; a file whose extension is not in the table, or that has none, such as a file still being downloaded (`.crdownload`, `.part`, `.download`) or a hidden file (`.DS_Store`); and each subfolder with what it holds.

AC6: After any run of AC3, AC4, AC9 or AC10, every file that was in the folder, its subfolders included, is either where it was before the run or where the run moved it, under the same name and with the same content; none is deleted, renamed or overwritten.

AC7: The repository holds automated tests that build a test folder with a file for each case of AC3 to AC6 and AC9 to AC11, check each of those criteria on it and pass, never touching the user's real Downloads folder or the user's own record of a last run.

AC8: The README says how to install the tool, show the planned moves, make the moves, work on another folder, show and make the moves back of an undo, and remove the tool, so that following it alone the user can run the tool on a test Downloads folder of their own making.

AC9: Asked to undo without being told to move, the tool shows each file the last run of AC4 on that folder moved, with where it would go back to, and each file it could not move back with the reason, and changes nothing in the folder.

AC10: Asked to undo and told to move, the tool moves each file the last run of AC4 on that folder moved back to where it was, and then removes each kind folder that run newly made and that is now empty; a kind folder holding anything, or one that was there before that run, stays.

AC11: In a run of AC9 or of AC10, a file stays where it is and is shown as not moved back, with the reason, when a file of the same name is now where it was or when it is no longer in its kind folder; the other files are moved back as AC10 says.

AC12: The tool keeps what each run of AC4 moved, from where to where, in a place of its own under the user's home (`~/.local/state/organize-downloads` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/organize-downloads` on macOS), one record for each folder, so the organized folder gains no file of the tool's.
